claims.text: Replacing EAM references with MLIPs trained on AIMD data for solid and liquid high-entropy-alloy configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap from the MLIP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references.
The intervention is to replace EAM references with MLIPs trained on AIMD data.
The proposed MLIPs will represent atomic configurations and interactions in both solid and liquid states better than EAM references.
MLIPs can capture complex atomic interactions and configurations more accurately than EAM.
EAM is limited by its fixed functional form and parameterization.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy calculations.
TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references exhibit thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing at least five principal elements.
The proposed method applies at temperatures near the alloys' melting points.
Applicability is limited to compositions and temperatures for which reliable AIMD data can be generated and suitable MLIPs can be trained.
The magnitude of the path-mismatch reduction is unknown without direct comparative calculations.
The hypothesis depends on MLIPs generalizing adequately across the target solid and liquid phase space.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing EAM- and MLIP-referenced TOR-TILD calculations for the same representative alloy near its melting temperature.
Failure of the MLIP reference to reduce path mismatch or improve free-energy accuracy relative to EAM would falsify the hypothesis.
